guideline_title: Eat a variety of foods to ensure a balanced diet
key_advice: Eat a mix of cereals/millets, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk/eggs/flesh foods, nuts and oilseeds; use the My Plate for the Day as the guide.

guideline_title: Ensure provision of extra food and healthcare to pregnant and lactating women
key_advice: Pregnant and lactating women need extra energy, protein and micronutrients (iron, folate, calcium) and regular antenatal care.

guideline_title: Ensure exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months and continue breastfeeding till two years and beyond
key_advice: Give only breast milk for the first 6 months, then continue breastfeeding along with complementary foods.

guideline_title: Start complementary feeding at completion of six months of age
key_advice: Introduce safe, age-appropriate, energy-dense home foods at 6 months while continuing breastfeeding.

guideline_title: Ensure adequate and appropriate diets for children and adolescents, both in health and sickness
key_advice: Children and teens need balanced meals, healthy snacks and extra care with feeding during illness.

guideline_title: Eat plenty of vegetables and fruits
key_advice: Eat a variety of vegetables (including green leafy) and fruits every day, preferably seasonal and local.

guideline_title: Ensure moderate use of edible oils and animal foods and the avoidance of ghee/vanaspati/trans fats
key_advice: Use oils in moderation, vary the oils, limit visible fat, and avoid vanaspati and trans fats.

guideline_title: Avoid ultra-processed foods rich in fat, sugar and salt
key_advice: Limit packaged snacks, sugary drinks, instant foods and bakery items high in fat, sugar and salt.

guideline_title: Choose whole grains, millets and legumes for fibre and protein
key_advice: Prefer whole grains, millets and pulses over refined cereals to improve fibre and protein quality.

guideline_title: Use salt in moderation
key_advice: Cut down on added salt, pickles, papad and processed foods to lower blood pressure risk.
number_limit: Under 5 g salt per day (verify page)

guideline_title: Limit sugar intake
key_advice: Limit added sugar in tea, coffee, sweets and sweetened drinks.
number_limit: 20-25 g added sugar per day (per project brief; verify page)

guideline_title: Drink adequate and safe water
key_advice: Drink enough safe water through the day; more in hot weather and during physical activity.

guideline_title: Adopt healthy cooking practices
key_advice: Prefer steaming, boiling, pressure-cooking and roasting; avoid repeatedly reheated oil and charring.

guideline_title: Be physically active and maintain a healthy body weight
key_advice: Do regular physical activity and keep body weight in the healthy range.

guideline_title: Ensure food safety and hygiene
key_advice: Wash hands, store and cook food safely and avoid contaminated food and water.

guideline_title: Be cautious about dietary supplements and protein powders
key_advice: Most healthy people can meet protein needs from a balanced diet; supplements are not usually needed without medical advice.

guideline_title: Read information on food labels to make informed and healthy food choices
key_advice: Check ingredient list, nutrition information and claims before buying packaged foods.

guideline_title: Food label: read the ingredient list
key_advice: Ingredients are listed in descending order by weight; look for sugar, salt and fat names near the top.

guideline_title: Food label: check nutrition information per serving
key_advice: Compare sugar, salt (sodium) and fat per serving or per 100 g, and check the serving size.

guideline_title: Food label: treat front-of-pack claims with caution
key_advice: Claims such as 'natural', 'light' or 'immunity' do not mean a food is healthy; verify with the nutrition table.
